book_intro:
Blue Letter Bible bakanlığı ve BLB Enstitüsü, Kutsal Yazıların tahrif edilemezliğine olan kesin inancı da içeren tarihsel, muhafazakar Hristiyan inancına bağlıdır. BLB tarafından sağlanan metin ve ses içeriği bir dizi Evanjelik geleneği temsil ettiğinden, kaynak materyallerde aktarılan tüm fikir ve ilkelerin bu bakanlık tarafından toplamda onaylanması gerekmez.

notes.text: If Abishalom is the same as David’s son Absalom, one should remember that the Hebrew terms daughter and father (as well as “mother,” v. 10) do not necessarily refer to a first-generation relationship; they can mean “granddaughter,” etc.
a lamp in Jerusalem. See note on 11:34–39.
there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam . . . between Abijam and Jeroboam. The feud that began in ch. 12 between the houses of Rehoboam and Jeroboam continues.
Asa reigned forty-one years, from 910 to 869 b.c. On the generations depicted by mother, daughter, and father, see note on vv. 2–3.
He put away the male cult prostitutes. See note on 14:24.

The queen mother served as an adviser of the king and as teacher of the royal children. abominable image for Asherah. This is another object associated with the worship of the goddess Asherah like the Asherim mentioned in 14:15, 23. On the brook Kidron, see note on 2 Chron. 15:16.

Even though the high places were not taken away, Asa was commended for his religious policy. He was faithful enough to bring into the house of the Lord the sacred gifts of his father and his own sacred gifts. When 2 Chron. 14:3 says that Asa removed the high places, this should be taken as meaning he removed some but not all of them (compare 2 Chron. 15:17).
Baasha king of Israel finds Asa’s military position so weak that he is able to push into Benjamin and build up Ramah, only a few miles north of Jerusalem.

Asa took all the silver and the gold. Asa was forced to send a large bribe to Damascus to try to establish a new treaty like the one between his father Abijah and the previous Syrian king Tabrimmon (see note on 2 Chron. 16:2–5).
He left to the house of Jeroboam not one that breathed. Baasha fulfills the prophecy of 14:10–11.
